title: Fusion-assisted decoding of non-Abelian topological order
authors: Rohith Sajith, Yabo Li, Zijian Song, Tsung-Cheng Lu, Carolyn Zhang
abstract: Maximum likelihood (ML) decoders perform quantum error correction by measuring a set of syndromes, classically computing an optimal recovery based on these syndromes and the noise model, and then performing that recovery. ML decoders are well understood for the toric code and generalize straightforwardly to other surface codes with Abelian anyons, where they can saturate information-theoretic decoding thresholds. On the other hand, codes with non-Abelian anyons have become increasingly relevant because they can support transversal or constant-depth non-Clifford gates and admit efficient preparation protocols in modern quantum devices. However, they present new challenges for decoding: non-Abelian anyons cannot in general be deterministically annihilated, and the logical operators cannot be classified by Abelian homology. In this work, we show that refined syndrome sets, including measurements that resolve non-Abelian anyon fusion outcomes, systematically improve the performance of ML decoders. We demonstrate this concretely by constructing explicit decoders for the $D_4$ quantum double model under charge noise, and obtaining numerical results for thresholds via mappings to classical statistical-mechanics models. We show that there is a nonzero noise threshold below which the entire logical qudit can be recovered with a single round of measurements.
summary: This paper advances quantum error correction theory by developing improved Maximum Likelihood decoders for topological codes based on non-Abelian anyons. The authors show that incorporating measurements of anyon fusion outcomes significantly boosts the noise threshold for recovering the logical information. This work is crucial for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation using advanced topological materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of developing and improving Maximum Likelihood (ML) decoders for quantum error correction in topological quantum memories based on non-Abelian anyons.
main_result: By incorporating refined syndrome sets that measure non-Abelian anyon fusion outcomes, the ML decoder performance is systematically improved, allowing for the single-shot recovery of the central logical qudit up to a non-zero noise threshold.
method: The authors analyze the decoding problem by mapping it to classical statistical-mechanics models and constructing explicit decoders for specific non-Abelian models, such as the $D_4$ quantum double.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum memories exhibiting non-Abelian topological order, modeled using quantum double groups (e.g., $D_4$) on a cylinder geometry under charge noise. The decoding process involves measuring various syndrome sets, including local excitations and pair-fusion outcomes.
key_observables: Decoding thresholds ($p_c$), the purity of the logical state ($	ext{Tr}(ho^2)$), and the coherence information $I^{(2)}_{c,d}$.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($p$), the structure of the non-Abelian group ($D_4$), and the type of syndrome measurement used ($S(1), S(2), S(3)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that refining syndrome sets by measuring fusion outcomes systematically improves performance, although this comes at the cost of potentially losing information outside the central qudit.

paper_structure: The paper systematically defines the non-Abelian model, calculates the probabilities associated with different syndrome measurements ($S(1), S(2), S(3)$), and then focuses on deriving the ML decoders and calculating the resulting noise thresholds for the central qudit.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, advanced techniques for error correction beyond the well-understood Abelian case, directly impacting the feasibility of building topological quantum computers using exotic anyonic excitations.
